page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.medium is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a single dedicated 64-bit ARM core from the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family clocked at 2.8 GHz, provisioned as one vCPU. The compute core includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and shares 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data, and features no hardware acceleration GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of a single-core execution environment. Single-threaded performance lands in the middle tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1750.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1695.3. Decompression throughput is comparatively high, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression achieving 14.2 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale directly with the single available core, resulting in bottom-decile scores across multi-core Geekbench (1749.0), PassMark CPU (986.57), and multi-core stress-ng. Memory throughput records 115.6 GB/sec for small cached reads, tapering to 30.44 GB/sec for uncached reads and 11.7 GB/sec for large block writes. Application-level throughput shows 2.26 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.49 GB/sec in static web serving.

From an architectural standpoint, the m8gb.medium provides cost-efficient entry into the ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture without shared-core burst constraints, offering dedicated compute time. However, resource limitations preclude intensive enterprise workloads. The absence of local disk drives, modest 4.0 GB memory footprint, and lack of x86 vector extensions (AVX/AMX) establish a distinct tradeoff favoring low-concurrency lightweight operations over parallel compute. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, basic web serving, utility cron jobs, small database caching nodes, and continuous integration testing targeting arm64 architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.medium is a general-purpose, single-core cloud instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. Driven by an AWS Neoverse-V2 processor at 2.8 GHz, it provides 1 dedicated vCPU, 4.0 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes. Benchmark evaluations show solid single-threaded performance, including 14.2 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and a Geekbench single-core score of 1750.0, though overall multi-threaded output is bounded by the single vCPU configuration. Memory write bandwidth registers at 11.7 GB/sec on large blocks, while application benchmarks report 2.26 million Redis SET operations per second. The m8gb.medium represents a resource-efficient environment tailored for arm64 continuous integration tasks, lightweight web serving, microservices, and small background utility workloads.
